symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T\) is the fixed panel horizon.

symbols.name: calT
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T=\{1,\ldots,T\}\).

symbols.name: calG
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G\subseteq\{2,\ldots,T,\infty\}\) contains every retained adoption cohort and the never-adopting label \(\infty\).

symbols.name: Xspace
symbols.def: \(\mathcal X\) is the support of pretreatment covariates.

symbols.name: Ypot
symbols.def: \(Y_t(a,s)\) is the period-\(t\) outcome under enabling date \(a\) for eligibility state \(s\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: \(G\) is the first enabling date, with \(G=\infty\) for never enabling.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: \(S=1\) denotes treatment eligibility.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X\) is observed before any retained adoption date.

symbols.name: Wstar
symbols.space: \(\mathsf W^*=\mathbb R^{\mathcal T\times\mathcal G\times\{0,1\}}\times\mathcal G\times\{0,1\}\times\mathcal X\)
symbols.def: \(\mathsf W^*\) supports the potential-outcome array, cohort, eligibility, and covariates.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: \(Y_t=Y_t(G,S)\) is the realized period-\(t\) outcome.

symbols.name: Ospace
symbols.def: \(\mathsf O\) supports the observed panel, cohort, eligibility, and covariates.

symbols.name: O
symbols.def: \(O\) is one observed fixed-horizon panel unit.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q\) is the joint law of \(Y_t(a,s)\), \(G\), \(S\), and \(X\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: \(P\) is a probability law for the observed panel vector \(O\).

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: \(n\) is the number of sampled panel units.

symbols.name: Icell
symbols.def: \(\mathbf 1_{a,u}=\mathbf 1\{G=a,S=u\}\) for \(a\in\mathcal G\) and \(u\in\{0,1\}\).

symbols.name: On
symbols.def: \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) is sampled from \(P\).

symbols.name: calK
symbols.def: \(\mathcal K\) is the prespecified set of group--time target indices \(k=(g,t)\).

symbols.name: calJ
symbols.type: family of nonempty finite comparison sets
symbols.def: For \(k=(g,t)\), \(\mathcal J_k\) contains every prespecified clean cohort \(c\in\mathcal G\) satisfying \(c>t\).

symbols.name: c0
symbols.def: For each \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(c_0(k)\) is a prespecified element of \(\mathcal J_k\).

symbols.name: calI
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I=\{(k,c):k\in\mathcal K,\ c\in\mathcal J_k\}\).

symbols.name: Kdim
symbols.def: \(K_0=|\mathcal K|\).

symbols.name: Mdim
symbols.def: \(M=|\mathcal I|=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}|\mathcal J_k|\).

symbols.name: omega
symbols.def: \(\omega=(\omega_k)_{k\in\mathcal K}\) is fixed before observing the sample.

symbols.name: DeltaY
symbols.def: For \(u\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\), \(\Delta Y_u=Y_u-Y_{u-1}\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: \(p_{a,s}(x)=P(G=a,S=s\mid X=x)\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: \(m_{a,s,u}(x)=E_P[\Delta Y_u\mid G=a,S=s,X=x]\) for \(u\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\).

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: For the fixed reference comparison \(c_0(k)\in\mathcal J_k\), \(\theta_k(P)=E_P[p_{g,1}(X)q_{k,c_0(k)}(X)]/\pi_{g,1}\), where \(k=(g,t)\).

symbols.name: tauomega
symbols.def: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\omega^{\prime}\theta(P)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\theta_k(P)\).

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: \(A_{(k,c),\ell}=\mathbf 1\{k=\ell\}\).

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: The columns of \(N\) form an orthonormal basis of \(\ker(A^{\prime})\), with the zero-column convention when \(M=K_0\).

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: \(R_P(O)\) is the pairwise doubly robust score constructed in \(\mathrm{Def.}\ \(\ref{def:pairwise-score}\) from the observed-law primitives \(p\), \(m\), \(q\), and \(\pi\).

symbols.name: Psi
symbols.def: \(\Psi_P(O)=R_P(O)-A\theta(P)\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: For \(k=(g,t)\), \(h_k(x)=p_{g,1}(x)q_{k,c_0(k)}(x)/\pi_{g,1}-\theta_k(P)\); on the observable equality model this is unchanged if \(c_0(k)\) is replaced by any \(c\in\mathcal J_k\).

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: \(\Gamma_P(x)=\operatorname{Cov}_P\{R_P(O)\mid X=x\}\), retaining every cross-target covariance created by shared cohort--eligibility outcome cells.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: \(H_P(x)=N^{\prime}\operatorname{Cov}_P\{R_P(O)\mid X=x\}N=N^{\prime}\Gamma_P(x)N\).

symbols.name: calM
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M\) is the target-indexed staggered-DDD model constructed in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:target-model}\).

symbols.name: bbase
symbols.def: \(b^{0}=A(A^{\prime}A)^{-1}\omega\), so \(A^{\prime}b^{0}=\omega\).

symbols.name: bstar
symbols.def: \(b^{\star}(x)\) is the minimum-\(\Gamma(x)\)-seminorm element of \(\{b\in\mathbb R^M:A^{\prime}b=\omega\}\), selected orthogonally to \(\ker H(x)\) relative to \(b^0\).

symbols.name: phieff
symbols.def: \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O)=b^{\star}(X)^{\prime}\Psi(O)\).

symbols.name: Veff
symbols.def: \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}=E_P[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O)^2]\).

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: \(\Omega=E_P[\Psi(O)\Psi(O)^{\prime}]\).

symbols.name: bOVS
symbols.def: For each target block \(k\), let \(K_k=\begin{psmallmatrix}\Omega_{kk}&\mathbf 1\\\mathbf 1^{\prime}&0\end{psmallmatrix}\) and define \(\binom{b^{\mathrm{OVS}}_k}{\lambda_k}=K_k^{\dagger}\binom{0}{\omega_k}\). The Moore--Penrose solution is the minimum-Euclidean-norm member of the blockwise quadratic-program solution set; this convention remains defined when \(\Omega_{kk}\) is singular and reduces to \(\omega_k\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1/(\mathbf 1^{\prime}\Omega_{kk}^{-1}\mathbf 1)\) when \(\Omega_{kk}\) is nonsingular. The blocks are stacked in \(\mathcal I\)-order.

symbols.name: bconst
symbols.def: Let \(K_{\mathrm{const}}=\begin{psmallmatrix}\Omega&A\\A^{\prime}&0\end{psmallmatrix}\) and define \(\binom{b^{\mathrm{const}}}{\lambda_{\mathrm{const}}}=K_{\mathrm{const}}^{\dagger}\binom{0}{\omega}\). Equivalently, \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\) is the minimum-Euclidean-norm member of \(\arg\min_{A^{\prime}b=\omega}b^{\prime}\Omega b\).

symbols.name: bcmp
symbols.def: \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\) denotes either named constant comparator.

symbols.name: dcmp
symbols.def: \(d_{\mathrm{cmp}}(x)=N^{\prime}\Gamma(x)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\).

symbols.name: Deltafun
symbols.def: For feasible \(b\), \(\Delta(b)=\operatorname{Var}_P\{b^{\prime}\Psi(O)\}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}\).

symbols.name: DeltaCmp
symbols.def: \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)=E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}})^{\prime}\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^{\star}(X)^{\prime}\Gamma_P(X)b^{\star}(X)]\), where \(\Omega_P=E_P[\Gamma_P(X)+Ah_P(X)h_P(X)^{\prime}A^{\prime}]\) determines \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\) through its declared Moore--Penrose KKT system.

symbols.name: Tang
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T_P\) is the closed span of scores of regular observed-law submodels induced by full-data laws in the target-indexed DDD model.

symbols.name: Cclosure
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_P=\overline{\{a(X)^{\prime}N^{\prime}R_P(O):a\text{ measurable and }E_P[(a(X)^{\prime}N^{\prime}R_P(O))^2]<\infty\}}^{L_2(P)}\).

symbols.name: folds
symbols.def: \((I_\ell)_{\ell=1}^L\) is a fixed-\(L\) cross-fitting partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

symbols.name: phat
symbols.def: \(\widehat p^{-\ell}\) is trained outside validation fold \(I_\ell\) and clipped inside the overlap interval.

symbols.name: mhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat m^{-\ell}\) estimates the one-step regressions \(m_{a,s,u}\) using observations outside validation fold \(I_\ell\).

symbols.name: Gammahat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)\) estimates \(\operatorname{Cov}_P\{R_P(O)\mid X=x\}\), including every shared-cell covariance, and is symmetrized on the training sample.

symbols.name: taun
symbols.def: \(\tau_n\downarrow0\) is fixed before sampling and thresholds foldwise eigenvalues of \(N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N\).

symbols.name: Hhat
symbols.def: Let \(\widehat H_{\mathrm{raw}}^{-\ell}(x)=N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N\). The foldwise rank selector is \(\widehat r^{-\ell}(x)=\#\{j:\lambda_j(\widehat H_{\mathrm{raw}}^{-\ell}(x))>\tau_n\}\), and \(\widehat H^{-\ell}(x)\) retains exactly those eigencomponents, with Moore--Penrose inverse formed from the retained eigenvalues; the zero-rank convention applies when no eigenvalue exceeds \(\tau_n\).

symbols.name: Omegahat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Omega^{-\ell}\) is the symmetrized empirical covariance of the cross-fitted joint score on the training complement of \(I_\ell\).

symbols.name: bcmphat
symbols.def: \(\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}}\) is obtained from \(\widehat\Omega^{-\ell}\) by the same Moore--Penrose KKT system and minimum-Euclidean-norm convention that defines \(b^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) or \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\).

symbols.name: dhatcmp
symbols.def: \(\widehat d^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}(x)=N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}}\).

symbols.name: bhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat b^{-\ell}(x)=b^0-N\{\widehat H^{-\ell}(x)\}^{\dagger}N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)b^0\), which satisfies \(A^{\prime}\widehat b^{-\ell}(x)=\omega\) exactly.

symbols.name: Dprojhat
symbols.def: For \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\in\{b^{\mathrm{OVS}},b^{\mathrm{const}}\}\), \(\widehat d^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}(x)=N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)\widehat b^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}\), where the training-fold constant loading \(\widehat b^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}\) is computed from the corresponding Moore--Penrose KKT system with the minimum-Euclidean-norm tie break.

symbols.name: Rhat
symbols.def: For \(i\in I_\ell\), \(\widehat R_i\) is \(R(O_i)\) with \(p,m,\pi\) replaced by the off-fold learners and the empirical target-cell share.

symbols.name: tauhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}=n^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in I_\ell}\widehat b^{-\ell}(X_i)^{\prime}\widehat R_i\).

symbols.name: Vhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(\widehat\phi_i-\overline{\widehat\phi})^2\), where \(\widehat\phi_i=\widehat b^{-\ell}(X_i)^{\prime}\widehat R_i-\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\) for \(i\in I_\ell\).

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: \(\alpha\) is fixed.

symbols.name: CI
symbols.def: \(\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}=\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}/n}\).

symbols.name: rp
symbols.def: \(r_{p,n}\) indexes the off-fold propensity error.

symbols.name: rm
symbols.def: \(r_{m,n}\) indexes the off-fold regression error.

symbols.name: rGamma
symbols.def: \(r_{\Gamma,n}\) indexes the off-fold conditional-covariance error.

symbols.name: dX
symbols.def: \(d_X\) is the Euclidean dimension in the Hölder conditional-covariance regime.

symbols.name: betaGamma
symbols.def: \(\beta_{\Gamma}\) is the Hölder smoothness of every entry of the conditional shared-cell covariance.

symbols.name: JGamma
symbols.def: \(J_{\Gamma,n}\) is the tensor-spline or compactly supported wavelet dimension used to estimate \(\Gamma\).

symbols.name: rb
symbols.def: \(r_{b,n}=r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n\) is the conservative loading rate induced by thresholded Moore--Penrose inversion.

symbols.name: zetaDelta
symbols.type: canonical gradient of the gap functional
symbols.def: \(\zeta_{\Delta,b^{\mathrm{cmp}}}\in\mathcal T_P\) is the Riesz representer satisfying \(E_P[\zeta_{\Delta,b^{\mathrm{cmp}}}s]=\left.\partial_u\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P_u)\right|_{u=0}\) for every regular score \(s\in\mathcal T_P\).

symbols.name: Jseq
symbols.def: \(J_n\uparrow\infty\) indexes a prespecified bounded dictionary used to approximate the observed-law tangent space.

symbols.name: vJ
symbols.def: \(v_{J_n}=(v_1,\ldots,v_{J_n})^{\prime}\) is a prespecified dictionary whose centered union is dense in \(L_2^0(P)\).

symbols.name: Zcontrast
symbols.def: \(Z_P(O)=N^{\prime}R_P(O)\).

symbols.name: tJ
symbols.def: For each dictionary coordinate, \(t_{j,P}=v_j-E_P[v_j]-a_{j,P}(X)^{\prime}Z_P\), where \(a_{j,P}(x)=H_P(x)^{\dagger}E_P[Z_P(O)\{v_j(O)-E_P[v_j]\}\mid X=x]\); hence \(t_{j,P}\in\mathcal T_P\).

symbols.name: gDelta
symbols.def: Its coordinate \(j\) is the explicit observable pathwise derivative \(D\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},P}[t_{j,P}]\) defined in \(\mathrm{Def.}\ \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\)\).

symbols.name: zetaJ
symbols.def: \(\zeta_{\Delta,J_n,P}(O)=t_{J_n,P}(O)^{\prime}G_{J_n,P}^{\dagger}g_{\Delta,J_n,P}\), with the minimum-norm Moore--Penrose convention.

symbols.name: Deltahat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}=\sum_{\ell=1}^L |I_\ell|n^{-1}\left[\widetilde\Delta^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}+|I_\ell|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_\ell}\widehat\zeta^{-\ell}_{\Delta,J_n}(O_i)\right]\), where both displayed training-fold objects are given explicitly in \(\mathrm{Def.}\ \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\)\).

symbols.name: VDeltaHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}=n^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{i\in I_\ell}\{\widehat\zeta^{-\ell}_{\Delta,J_n}(O_i)-\overline{\widehat\zeta}_{\Delta}\}^2\), where \(\overline{\widehat\zeta}_{\Delta}=n^{-1}\sum_{\ell,i\in I_\ell}\widehat\zeta^{-\ell}_{\Delta,J_n}(O_i)\).

symbols.name: WaldDelta
symbols.def: \(T_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}=\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\}/\sqrt{\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}}\).

symbols.name: delta0
symbols.def: \(\delta_0\) separates the efficiency gap from its equality boundary.

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r\) indexes the covariate-reversing residual correlation in the strict-gain family.

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: \(\delta\) is the common nonzero post-adoption eligible effect in the witness family.

symbols.name: Uw
symbols.def: \(U^{\mathrm w}\) is the period-two residual sign in the binary witness.

symbols.name: Vw
symbols.def: \(V^{\mathrm w}\) is the period-three residual sign in the binary witness.

symbols.name: Zw
symbols.def: \(Z^{\mathrm w}=(0,U^{\mathrm w}/8,V^{\mathrm w}/8)^{\prime}\).

symbols.name: Qbin
symbols.def: \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\) is the bounded full-data construction in \(\mathrm{Def.}\) \(\ref{def:binary-witness}\).

symbols.name: lambdan
symbols.def: \(\lambda_n\downarrow0\) is a data-calibrated spectral threshold considered in the rank-adaptive extension.

assumptions.condition: \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed from \(P\), while \(T\) is fixed as \(n\to\infty\).
For every target cohort \(g\) represented in \(\mathcal K\) and every \(u\in\mathcal T\) with \(u<g\), \(E_Q[Y_u(g,1)-Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]=0\) almost surely.
\(Y_t(a,0)=Y_t(\infty,0)\) almost surely for every \(a\in\mathcal G\) and every \(t\in\mathcal T\).

standard.name: No treatment effect on ineligible units

assumptions.condition: For every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and every \(u\in\{g,\ldots,t\}\), \[E_Q[Y_u(\infty,1)-Y_{u-1}(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]-E_Q[Y_u(\infty,0)-Y_{u-1}(\infty,0)\mid G=g,S=0,X]\] equals \[E_Q[Y_u(\infty,1)-Y_{u-1}(\infty,1)\mid G=c,S=1,X]-E_Q[Y_u(\infty,0)-Y_{u-1}(\infty,0)\mid G=c,S=0,X]\] almost surely.

standard.name: OVS period-by-period covariate-conditional one-step DDD parallel trends

assumptions.condition: \(p_{a,s}(X)\ge\varepsilon\) almost surely for every cohort--eligibility cell \((a,s)\) used by at least one coordinate in \(\mathcal I\).
For every retained cohort--eligibility cell \((a,s)\) and every \(u\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\), \(E_P[|\Delta Y_u|^4\mid G=a,S=s,X]\le C_{4,c}\) almost surely.
Every positive eigenvalue of \(H(X)\) lies in \([\kappa,\kappa^{-1}]\) almost surely.

standard.name: Separated positive spectrum for a generalized-inverse system

assumptions.condition: Along every regular observed-law submodel used for efficiency-gap differentiation, the ranks of \(\begin{psmallmatrix}\Omega_{kk}&\mathbf 1\\\mathbf 1^{\prime}&0\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(k\in\mathcal K\), and \(\begin{psmallmatrix}\Omega&A\\A^{\prime}&0\end{psmallmatrix}\) are locally constant at \(P\).

standard.name: Local constant-rank condition for Moore--Penrose differentiation

assumptions.condition: Every positive singular value of each comparator KKT matrix \(\begin{psmallmatrix}\Omega_{kk}&\mathbf 1\\\mathbf 1^{\prime}&0\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(k\in\mathcal K\), and \(\begin{psmallmatrix}\Omega&A\\A^{\prime}&0\end{psmallmatrix}\) is at least \(\kappa_{\mathrm{cmp}}\).

standard.name: Separated positive spectrum for comparator KKT systems

assumptions.condition: For each \(I_\ell\), all nuisance, covariance, and loading evaluations on \(I_\ell\) are measurable with respect to observations outside \(I_\ell\).
\(\max_{\ell,a,s,u}\|\widehat m^{-\ell}_{a,s,u}-m_{a,s,u}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(r_{m,n})=o_P(1)\), where the maximum ranges over retained cells and \(u\in\{2,\ldots,T\}\).

novel.justification: This is a paper-specific sufficient estimation condition for the shared-cell DDD covariance, not a consequence attributed to the DiD literature. It is delivered by the finite-support and Hölder-series regimes in Proposition \(\ref{prop:covariance-learnability}\).
A deterministic vanishing threshold eventually retains every eigenvalue in the maintained positive spectral cluster.
A threshold dominating the conditional-covariance error consistently separates zero eigenvalues from sampling noise without treating \(r_0\) as known.

This paper-specific mixed rate controls the interaction of a threshold-selected conditional DDD loading with the propensity and outcome nuisances. The concrete covariance regimes and conventional nuisance rates make it checkable.
This paper-specific sufficient rate removes the quadratic error from estimating both the conditional covariance and its thresholded generalized-inverse loading in the efficiency-gap functional.

assumptions.condition: The positive eigenvalues of \(G_{J_n,P}\) lie in \([\underline g,\overline g]\) for fixed \(0<\underline g<\overline g<\infty\).

definitions.name: Target-indexed staggered-DDD model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{Q:Q\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:no\text{-}anticipation},\mathrm{ass:no\text{-}ineligible\text{-}effect},\text{ and }\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}parallel\text{-}gap}\}\), for the fixed finite \(T\), \(\mathcal K\), and every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\), \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), and \(u\in\{g,\ldots,t\}\).

definitions.name: Joint OVS score vector
definitions.construction: For \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\) and \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), let \(e_{a,s,k}(O)=\sum_{u=g}^t\{\Delta Y_u-m_{a,s,u}(X)\}\). Define the observed-law score \[R_{k,c,P}(O)=\frac{1}{\pi_{g,1}}\Bigg[\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}\{q_{k,c}(X)+e_{g,1,k}(O)\}-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{g,0}(X)}\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=0\}e_{g,0,k}(O)\] \[{}-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{c,1}(X)}\mathbf 1\{G=c,S=1\}e_{c,1,k}(O)+\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{p_{c,0}(X)}\mathbf 1\{G=c,S=0\}e_{c,0,k}(O)\Bigg],\qquad \Psi_{k,c,P}(O)=R_{k,c,P}(O)-\theta_k(P).\] Stack the coordinates in the fixed order \(\mathcal I\).

definitions.name: Fixed-rank conditional projection loading
definitions.construction: For almost every \(x\), \(b^{\star}(x)\) is selected from \(\arg\min_{b\in\mathbb R^M:A^{\prime}b=\omega}b^{\prime}\Gamma(x)b\) by requiring \(N^{\prime}\{b-b^0\}\in\operatorname{range}H(x)\).

definitions.name: Moore--Penrose comparator diagnostic
definitions.construction: For each training complement of \(I_\ell\), form \(\widehat\Omega^{-\ell}\). For the OVS comparator, solve each block KKT system \(\begin{psmallmatrix}\widehat\Omega^{-\ell}_{kk}&\mathbf 1\\\mathbf 1^{\prime}&0\end{psmallmatrix}\binom{v_k}{\lambda_k}=\binom{0}{\omega_k}\) by its Moore--Penrose inverse; for the joint constant comparator, solve \(\begin{psmallmatrix}\widehat\Omega^{-\ell}&A\\A^{\prime}&0\end{psmallmatrix}\binom{v}{\lambda}=\binom{0}{\omega}\) in the same way. In both cases take the minimum-Euclidean-norm loading component \(\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}}\) and report \(\widehat d^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}(x)=N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}}\).

definitions.name: Conditional-efficient cross-fitted estimator
definitions.construction: On each training complement of \(I_\ell\), estimate every retained \(p_{a,s}\), one-step regression \(m_{a,s,u}\), and shared-cell entry of \(\Gamma_P=\operatorname{Cov}_P(R_P\mid X)\). At each \(x\), count the eigenvalues of \(N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N\) above the deterministic \(\tau_n\), retain exactly those eigencomponents in \(\widehat H^{-\ell}(x)\), and form its Moore--Penrose inverse. Set \(\widehat b^{-\ell}=b^0-N\{\widehat H^{-\ell}\}^{\dagger}N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}b^0\), which enforces \(A^{\prime}\widehat b^{-\ell}=\omega\); evaluate \(\widehat R_i\) on \(I_\ell\); and return \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}=n^{-1}\sum_{\ell}\sum_{i\in I_\ell}\widehat b^{-\ell}(X_i)^{\prime}\widehat R_i\) with \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\) and \(\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\) as declared.

definitions.name: One-step efficiency-gap estimator
definitions.construction:
Write \(\mu_R(x)=E_P[R_P(O)\mid X=x]\) and \(L_P(x)=(b^{\mathrm{cmp}})^{\prime}\Gamma_P(x)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^{\star}(x)^{\prime}\Gamma_P(x)b^{\star}(x)\), so \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)=E_P[L_P(X)]\). For any mean-zero observed score \(s\), define \(\dot p_{a,u,s}(x)=E_P[(\mathbf 1\{G=a,S=u\}-p_{a,u}(x))s(O)\mid X=x]\), \(\dot m_{a,u,v,s}(x)=E_P[\mathbf 1\{G=a,S=u\}\{\Delta Y_v-m_{a,u,v}(x)\}s(O)\mid X=x]/p_{a,u}(x)\), and \(\dot\pi_{g,1,s}=E_P[(\mathbf 1\{G=g,S=1\}-\pi_{g,1})s(O)]\). For \(k=(g,t)\), \(\dot q_{k,c,s}=\sum_{v=g}^t(\dot m_{g,1,v,s}-\dot m_{g,0,v,s}-\dot m_{c,1,v,s}+\dot m_{c,0,v,s})\), and, writing \(
u_k=E_P[p_{g,1}(X)q_{k,c_0(k)}(X)]\), \(\dot	heta_{k,s}=\{E_P[(p_{g,1}q_{k,c_0(k)}-
u_k)s]+E_P[\dot p_{g,1,s}q_{k,c_0(k)}+p_{g,1}\dot q_{k,c_0(k),s}]\}/\pi_{g,1}-
u_k\dot\pi_{g,1,s}/\pi_{g,1}^2\). Put \(e_{a,u,k}=\sum_{v=g}^t(\Delta Y_v-m_{a,u,v})\), \(\dot e_{a,u,k,s}=-\sum_{v=g}^t\dot m_{a,u,v,s}\), \(w_{a,u}=p_{g,1}/p_{a,u}\), and \(\dot w_{a,u,s}=(\dot p_{g,1,s}p_{a,u}-p_{g,1}\dot p_{a,u,s})/p_{a,u}^2\). If \(F_{k,c}\) denotes the bracketed numerator in Definition \(ef{def:pairwise-score}\), then \[\dot F_{k,c,s}=\mathbf 1_{g,1}(\dot q_{k,c,s}+\dot e_{g,1,k,s})-\mathbf 1_{g,0}(\dot w_{g,0,s}e_{g,0,k}+w_{g,0}\dot e_{g,0,k,s})-\mathbf 1_{c,1}(\dot w_{c,1,s}e_{c,1,k}+w_{c,1}\dot e_{c,1,k,s})+\mathbf 1_{c,0}(\dot w_{c,0,s}e_{c,0,k}+w_{c,0}\dot e_{c,0,k,s}),\qquad \dot R_{k,c,s}=\dot F_{k,c,s}/\pi_{g,1}-R_{k,c}\dot\pi_{g,1,s}/\pi_{g,1}.\] Set \(\dot h_{k,s}=(\dot p_{g,1,s}q_{k,c_0(k)}+p_{g,1}\dot q_{k,c_0(k),s})/\pi_{g,1}-p_{g,1}q_{k,c_0(k)}\dot\pi_{g,1,s}/\pi_{g,1}^2-\dot	heta_{k,s}\), \(\dot\mu_{R,s}=E_P[(R_P-\mu_R)s\mid X]+E_P[\dot R_s\mid X]\), and \[\dot\Gamma_s=E_P[\{(R_P-\mu_R)(R_P-\mu_R)^{\prime}-\Gamma_P\}s\mid X]+E_P[(\dot R_s-\dot\mu_{R,s})(R_P-\mu_R)^{\prime}+(R_P-\mu_R)(\dot R_s-\dot\mu_{R,s})^{\prime}\mid X].\] Then \[\dot\Omega_s=E_P[\{\Gamma_P(X)+Ah(X)h(X)^{\prime}A^{\prime}-\Omega_P\}s]+E_P[\dot\Gamma_s(X)+A\{\dot h_s(X)h(X)^{\prime}+h(X)\dot h_s(X)^{\prime}\}A^{\prime}].\] For the applicable comparator KKT matrix \(K_P\) and fixed right-hand side \(y\), use \[D K_P^{\dagger}[E]=-K_P^{\dagger}EK_P^{\dagger}+K_P^{\dagger}K_P^{\dagger\prime}E^{\prime}(I-K_PK_P^{\dagger})+(I-K_P^{\dagger}K_P)E^{\prime}K_P^{\dagger\prime}K_P^{\dagger}\] with \(E\) the block insertion of \(\dot\Omega_s\); \(\dot b^{\mathrm{cmp}}_s\) is the loading block of \(D K_P^{\dagger}[E]y\), block by block for OVS. Local constant KKT rank makes this derivative valid. The exact pathwise derivative, with the pointwise optimizer term removed by its envelope equation and the comparator term retained, is \[D\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp},P}[s]=E_P[\{L_P(X)-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\}s]+E_P[\operatorname{tr}\{(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}b^{\mathrm{cmp}\prime}-b^{\star}(X)b^{\star}(X)^{\prime})\dot\Gamma_s(X)\}]+2E_P[\{\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\}^{\prime}\dot b^{\mathrm{cmp}}_s].\] Start with the bounded dictionary \(v_{J_n}\). On each training complement, estimate \(Z=N^{\prime}R\), \(H\), and \(E[Z\{v_j-Ev_j\}\mid X]\); form \(\widehat t_j^{-\ell}=v_j-\mathbb E_{-\ell}v_j-\widehat a_j^{-\ell}(X)^{\prime}\widehat Z\), where \(\widehat a_j^{-\ell}=\{\widehat H^{-\ell}\}^{\dagger}\widehat E_{-\ell}[\widehat Z\{v_j-\mathbb E_{-\ell}v_j\}\mid X]\), and center it on the training fold. Replace \(p,m,q,\pi,	heta,R,h,\Gamma,\Omega,b^{\star},b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\) in every displayed directional formula by their training-fold estimates and replace conditional expectations by the same finite-support or series regressions used for \(\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}\). Evaluation at \(s=\widehat t_j^{-\ell}\) gives \(\widehat g^{-\ell}_{\Delta,J_n}\), while \(\widehat G^{-\ell}_{J_n}=\mathbb E_{-\ell}[\widehat t^{-\ell}_{J_n}\widehat t^{-\ell\prime}_{J_n}]\) and \(\widehat\zeta^{-\ell}_{\Delta,J_n}(O)=\widehat t^{-\ell}_{J_n}(O)^{\prime}\{\widehat G^{-\ell}_{J_n}\}^{\dagger}\widehat g^{-\ell}_{\Delta,J_n}\). The training plug-in is \[\widetilde\Delta^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}=\mathbb E_{-\ell}[(\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}})^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(X)\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}}-\widehat b^{-\ell}(X)^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(X)\widehat b^{-\ell}(X)].\] Aggregate \(\widetilde\Delta^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}+|I_\ell|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_\ell}\widehat\zeta^{-\ell}_{\Delta,J_n}(O_i)\) with weights \(|I_\ell|/n\), and compute \(\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\) and \(T_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\) as declared.

definitions.name: Bounded binary-covariate strict-gain family
definitions.construction: Set \(T=3\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,2),(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,2)}=\{3,\infty\}\), and \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{\infty\}\). Draw \(X\) uniformly on \(\{-1,1\}\), and draw \((G,S)\) uniformly on \(\{2,3,\infty\}\times\{0,1\}\) conditional on \(X\). Conditional on \(X=x\) and \(G=a\), draw \((U^{\mathrm w},V^{\mathrm w})\in\{-1,1\}^2\) with probability \(\{1+\rho_a(x)U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\}/4\), where \(\rho_2(x)=\rho_3(x)=0\) and \(\rho_{\infty}(x)=xr\). Put \(Z^{\mathrm w}=(0,U^{\mathrm w}/8,V^{\mathrm w}/8)^{\prime}\), define \(Y_t(a,s)=Z_t^{\mathrm w}+\delta s\mathbf 1\{a<\infty\}\mathbf 1\{t\ge a\}\), and set \(Y_t=Y_t(G,S)\). The resulting full-data law is \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\).

definitions.name: Rank-adaptive spectral handle
definitions.construction: Use cross-fitted spectral projectors for \(H(X)\), select \(\lambda_n\) by a Lepski-type stability comparison across adjacent eigenspaces, preserve \(A^{\prime}b=\omega\) by affine projection, and combine directional delta-method critical values across the retained rank candidates to target a confidence interval for \(\tau_{\omega}\).

statements.statement: Fix \(\mathcal K\), \((\mathcal J_k)_{k\in\mathcal K}\), and \(c_0(k)\in\mathcal J_k\). For an observed law \(P\), construct \(p\), \(m\), \(q\), \(\pi\), \(\theta(P)\), and \(R_P\) solely from the observed distribution, and set \(\Gamma_P(x)=\operatorname{Cov}_P\{R_P(O)\mid X=x\}\) and \(H_P(x)=N^{\prime}\Gamma_P(x)N\). Suppose retained-cell overlap and the fourth-moment envelope hold, \(\operatorname{rank}H_P(X)=r_0\) almost surely, and every positive eigenvalue of \(H_P(X)\) lies in \([\kappa,\kappa^{-1}]\). Then \(P\) admits a full-data extension \(Q\in\mathcal M\) inducing \(P\) if and only if \[q_{k,c}(X)=q_{k,c_0(k)}(X)\quad P_X\text{-almost surely for every }k\in\mathcal K\text{ and }c\in\mathcal J_k.\] At every regular interior \(P\) satisfying these observable equalities, \(N^{\prime}R_P\) has conditional mean zero and the induced observed-law tangent space obeys \[\mathcal T_P^{\perp}=\mathcal C_P.\] Hence every regular gradient of \(\tau_{\omega}(P)\) differs from one fixed pairwise gradient by exactly one element of \(\mathcal C_P\).
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing local full-data-to-observed equivalence that turns score-family optimization into semiparametric efficiency.
statements.gap: Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2) give the analogous observable conditional-moment characterizations for single-date and staggered DiD; they do not establish the DDD-only full-data extension or exhaust the coupled eligibility-gap tangent space with shared histories and target-share derivatives.
statements.consumer: The theorem certifies whether the conditional loading can be called canonical and whether overidentifying restrictions support specification tests.

statements.statement: Let \(P\) satisfy the observable clean-comparison equalities and admit \(Q\in\mathcal M\) that induces \(P\). For every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\) and every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\), \[q_{k,c}(X)=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.\] Consequently, the already-defined observable functional obeys \[\theta_k(P)=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1],\qquad \tau_{\omega}(P)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_k\theta_k(P),\] and \(\Psi_P=R_P-A\theta(P)\) is the centered full-data-compatible OVS score vector.
statements.justification: This fixes the causal target before any efficiency calculation and retains the denominator derivative through \(\pi_{g,1}\).
statements.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorem 4.1) establish identification under their conditional-mean no-anticipation and period-by-period DDD parallel-trends conditions; this lemma records the exact reduction used here rather than claiming novelty.
statements.consumer: Every later tangent, score, and package result targets the same prespecified aggregate rather than a data-adaptive estimand.

statements.statement: Under fixed contrast rank, the conditional minimizer has the measurable quotient-space representation \[b^{\star}(x)=b^0-NH(x)^{\dagger}N^{\prime}\Gamma(x)b^0,\] satisfies \(A^{\prime}b^{\star}(x)=\omega\) and \(N^{\prime}\Gamma(x)b^{\star}(x)=0\), and is unique modulo \(\ker\Gamma(x)\cap\ker A^{\prime}\). The range relation \(N^{\prime}\Gamma(x)b^0\in\operatorname{range}H(x)\) follows from positive semidefiniteness and is not assumed. If \(\Gamma(x)\) is positive definite, then \[b^{\star}(x)=\Gamma(x)^{-1}A\{A^{\prime}\Gamma(x)^{-1}A\}^{-1}\omega.\]
statements.justification: Redundant clean comparisons are economically natural, so the efficient loading must be invariant to null score coordinates.
statements.gap: Newey (2001, Theorem 5.2) handles singular conditional-moment covariance abstractly; the result here supplies the DDD affine-constraint quotient and its measurable fixed-rank form.
statements.consumer: The constrained solver used by the optional \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend remains defined when retained score coordinates are redundant.

statements.statement: At every regular interior \(P\) in the observable target-indexed staggered-DDD model, \[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O)=b^{\star}(X)^{\prime}\Psi_P(O)\] is the canonical gradient of \(\tau_{\omega}(P)\). Its variance is \[V_{\mathrm{eff}}=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega^{\prime}h(X)\}+E_P[b^{\star}(X)^{\prime}\Gamma_P(X)b^{\star}(X)],\] and every regular asymptotically linear estimator has asymptotic variance at least \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}\). This strictly tightens the OVS constant componentwise GMM benchmark whenever its pointwise projection equation fails.
statements.justification: The result identifies the full observed-law information bound for a joint finite aggregate rather than the optimum inside a prespecified score span.
statements.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorem 4.2 and Remark 4.6) establish asymptotic normality and optimize constant within-target GMM weights; Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, Theorem 3.2) derive the optimal conditional efficient influence function and bound for staggered DiD, while their Theorem 4.1 proves attainment, but neither result contains the DDD-only full-data extension or coupled eligibility-gap tangent-exhaustion step.
statements.consumer: Applied researchers obtain the correct precision benchmark and a principled reason to retain every admissible clean cohort.

statements.statement: The paper-specific covariance and threshold rates are attainable in two concrete regimes. First, if \(X\) has fixed finite support with every support mass bounded below, the foldwise cell-frequency covariance of the cross-fitted \(\widehat R\) has \(r_{\Gamma,n}=n^{-1/2}+r_{p,n}+r_{m,n}\) in \(L_4(P_X)\); all conditional expectations in Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\) are estimated by the corresponding cell averages. With parametric first stages and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), any \(0<a<1/4\) gives consistent rank recovery and \(r_{b,n}=O(n^{-1/2+a})\). Second, suppose \(X\in[0,1]^{d_X}\) has density bounded above and away from zero, every entry of \(\Gamma\) and every conditional expectation displayed in Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\), uniformly over \(j\le J_n\), lies in a common \(\beta_{\Gamma}\)-Hölder ball with \(\beta_{\Gamma}>d_X/2\), and the conditional fourth-moment envelope holds. A tensor-spline or compactly supported wavelet least-squares estimator with \(J_{\Gamma,n}\asymp n^{d_X/(2\beta_{\Gamma}+d_X)}\) then gives \[r_{\Gamma,n}=O\!\left(n^{-\beta_{\Gamma}/(2\beta_{\Gamma}+d_X)}+r_{p,n}+r_{m,n}\right).\] If \(J_nJ_{\Gamma,n}/n\to0\), the same regressions make the projected-score sample equations and all coordinates of \(\widehat g_{\Delta,J_n}\) consistent. When first-stage errors do not dominate and \(\tau_n=r_{\Gamma,n}^{a}\) for any \(0<a<1/2-d_X/(4\beta_{\Gamma})\), the selected rank is consistent, \(r_{b,n}=O(r_{\Gamma,n}^{1-a})\), and the quadratic covariance/loading condition holds. In either regime, the mixed condition follows whenever \(r_{p,n}+r_{m,n}=o(n^{-1/2}/r_{b,n})\).
statements.justification: The abstract rate conditions are credible only if familiar discrete-cell and smooth-regression learners deliver them with explicit tuning ranges.
statements.gap: Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025) do not estimate the full shared-cell DDD conditional covariance in \(L_4(P_X)\); this proposition supplies paper-specific sufficient regimes rather than attributing that rate to their DiD theorem.
statements.consumer: Implementers can select either cell-frequency covariance estimates for discrete covariates or a transparent smooth series learner for continuous covariates.

statements.statement: Let \(\widehat r^{-\ell}(x)=\#\{j:\lambda_j(N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N)>\tau_n\}\), and form \(\widehat H^{-\ell}\) and \(\widehat b^{-\ell}\) from the retained eigencomponents. Under fixed rank, separated positive spectrum, \(L_4(P_X)\) covariance error, and \(r_{\Gamma,n}=o(\tau_n)\), \(P_X\{\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\ne r_0\}=O_P\{(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n)^4\}\) uniformly over folds. The thresholded Moore--Penrose perturbation and its projector obey \[\max_{\ell}\|\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^{\star}\|_{P_X,2}+\max_{\ell}\|\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^{\star}\|_{P_X,4}=O_P(r_{b,n})=o_P(1),\qquad r_{b,n}=r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n.\] On the consistently selected spectral range the sharper local bound is \(O_P(r_{\Gamma,n})\). Thus both rank recovery and the loading rate are derived from covariance learning and threshold separation rather than supplied by an oracle rank or a standalone loading assumption.
statements.justification: The learned loading rate must follow from covariance estimation and stable quotient geometry rather than being assumed as an independent first-stage property.
statements.gap: Standard Moore--Penrose perturbation bounds do not by themselves control the DDD loading in \(L_4(P_X)\); the conditional moment envelope and the affine fixed-rank construction close that step.
statements.consumer: The result supplies the loading remainder bound used by both the efficient estimator and the efficiency-gap estimator.

statements.statement: Under the stated sampling, overlap, fourth-moment, fixed-rank, spectral, cross-fitting, nuisance, covariance, threshold, and product-rate conditions, the foldwise selector \(\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\) consistently recovers \(r_0\) in \(P_X\)-probability without treating \(r_0\) as known. The loading perturbation lemma then yields \[\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_{\omega})=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_P(1),\qquad \widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\to_PV_{\mathrm{eff}}.\] If \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}>0\), then \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_{\omega})/\sqrt{\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\) and \(P\{\tau_{\omega}\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: Canonicality has operational value only if conditional shared-cell covariance and its loading can be learned without a first-order penalty.
statements.gap: Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, Theorem 5) derive the panel DDD efficient influence function, while their Theorem 7 treats repeated cross-sections and Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Theorem 3.1) give generic DML; none controls a learned all-cohort panel-DDD covariance loading.
statements.consumer: The theorem supplies the statistical contract for an optional efficient backend in the CRAN package \(\texttt{triplediff}\).

statements.statement: For either globally defined Moore--Penrose comparator \(b\in\{b^{\mathrm{OVS}},b^{\mathrm{const}}\}\), \[\Delta(b)=E_P[(b-b^{\star}(X))^{\prime}\Gamma(X)(b-b^{\star}(X))].\] Under the separated positive spectrum on the contrast range, \(\Delta(b)=0\) if and only if \[d_{\mathrm{cmp}}(X)=N^{\prime}\Gamma(X)b=0\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.\] Thus the published OVS loading and the best joint constant loading are efficient exactly when each satisfies its own pointwise projection equations; unconditional cancellation is insufficient. The observable plug-in residual is \(\widehat d^{-\ell}_{\mathrm{cmp}}(x)=N^{\prime}\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)\widehat b^{-\ell,\mathrm{cmp}}\), with each comparator recomputed by the same Moore--Penrose KKT and minimum-norm convention.
statements.justification: The pointwise equations give a falsifiable equality frontier rather than a generic claim that conditional weighting helps.
statements.gap: The banked constant-loading parent derives only an unconditional normal equation, and Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025) do not characterize equality with the conditional efficiency bound.
statements.consumer: An empirical diagnostic can determine whether the published package backend already attains the bound at the fitted law.

statements.statement: For either globally defined Moore--Penrose comparator \(b^{\mathrm{cmp}}\in\{b^{\mathrm{OVS}},b^{\mathrm{const}}\}\), \[\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)=E_P[(b^{\mathrm{cmp}})^{\prime}\Gamma_P(X)b^{\mathrm{cmp}}-b^{\star}(X)^{\prime}\Gamma_P(X)b^{\star}(X)].\] Its pathwise derivative is the fully displayed observable formula in Definition \(\ref{def:gap-one-step}\): it includes \(\dot\Gamma_s\), the Moore--Penrose KKT derivative \(\dot b^{\mathrm{cmp}}_s\), and the envelope cancellation for \(\dot b^{\star}_s\). Under the stated sieve dimension, Gram-spectrum, and approximation conditions, the training-fold projected scores satisfy \(\|\widehat\zeta^{-\ell}_{\Delta,J_n}-\zeta_{\Delta,b^{\mathrm{cmp}}}\|_{P,2}=o_P(1)\). At every fixed law with locally constant comparator-KKT ranks, separated positive comparator-KKT singular values, and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\ge\delta_0>0\), \[\sqrt n\{\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}-\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\zeta_{\Delta,b^{\mathrm{cmp}}}(O_i)+o_P(1),\qquad \widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\to_P E_P[\zeta_{\Delta,b^{\mathrm{cmp}}}(O)^2].\] If this variance is positive, \(T_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\), and the interval \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_{\Delta,\mathrm{cmp}}/n}\) has pointwise coverage \(1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: The efficiency comparison becomes empirically interpretable only when sampling uncertainty in the optimized variance loss is quantified.
statements.gap: Sant'Anna and Xu (2026) construct a Hausman comparison for regular DiD estimators; they do not derive inference for an optimized conditional-versus-constant DDD variance functional.
statements.consumer: A \(\texttt{triplediff}\) user can report whether an estimated precision gain is separated from zero rather than comparing standard errors informally.

statements.statement: For every \(0<r<\sqrt7/3\), \(0<|\delta|<1/8\), and \(\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2)^{\prime}\) with \(\omega_2\ne0\), the law \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\). In score order \(((2,2),3),((2,2),\infty),((2,3),\infty)\), \[\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix},\qquad b^{\star}(x)=\begin{pmatrix}\omega_1/2+xr\omega_2/2\\\omega_1/2-xr\omega_2/2\\\omega_2\end{pmatrix}.\] The conditional eigenvalues are \(3/8\) and \(3\{2\pm\sqrt{1+r^2}\}/16\), so the smallest exceeds \(1/8\). Both constant comparators equal \((\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)^{\prime}\), and \[\Delta(b^{\mathrm{OVS}})=\Delta(b^{\mathrm{const}})=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0.\] At \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), the exact gain is \(3/512\).
statements.justification: An open bounded family shows that the conditional gain is structural, not a singularity or one-law artifact.
statements.gap: The banked parent exhibits a constant-covariate joint-loading gain; the sign-reversing binary mixture is the first construction in which every constant loading loses to covariate-adaptive weighting.
statements.consumer: The family is the symbolic early-kill test for tangent exhaustion and a reproducible unit test for software implementation.

statements.statement: If every \(\mathcal J_k\) is a singleton, then \(M=K_0\), \(N\) has no columns, and \(b^{\star}\) is the unique feasible loading; for a single two-period panel target the resulting \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\) equals the panel-DDD efficient influence function in Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, Theorem 5). If \(X\) is degenerate, then \(\Gamma_P(X)\) is constant and \(b^{\star}(X)=b^{\mathrm{const}}\) almost surely.
statements.justification: These reductions check the operator formula against the just-identified DDD EIF and the completed constant-loading geometry.
statements.gap: Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, Theorem 5) supply the panel-DDD efficient influence function, and the constant-covariate score geometry supplies the second reduction; both must be exact special cases.
statements.consumer: The reductions provide regression tests for mathematical derivations and the package backend.

statements.statement: Can the rank-adaptive spectral handle construct an estimator of \(\tau_{\omega}\) and a confidence interval with uniform asymptotic coverage over laws for which the smallest positive eigenvalue of \(H(X)\) approaches zero and the conditional rank changes on sets of positive probability, while reducing to \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\) on every fixed-rank separated law?
statements.justification: Rank changes are the natural nonregular boundary of the proposed efficiency theory and cannot be hidden inside a fixed-rank assumption.
statements.gap: Newey (2001) gives generalized-inverse optimality under a stable conditional system, while the staggered DiD and DDD literatures do not provide rank-adaptive inference for learned conditional weights.
statements.consumer: A rank-adaptive procedure would prevent unstable standard errors when empirical clean-comparison scores are nearly redundant.

sampling_model.design: Observational staggered adoption in a balanced fixed-\(T\) panel under the OVS target-indexed, period-by-period covariate-conditional one-step DDD parallel-trends restrictions.
sampling_model.units: \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed panel units.
sampling_model.treatment: Enabling is absorbing through cohort \(G\), and effective treatment requires \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort--eligibility cell entering a retained clean comparison has conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates cell propensities, outcome-change regressions, and the full shared-cell conditional covariance. A deterministic vanishing eigenvalue threshold selects the conditional contrast rank, Moore--Penrose perturbation derives the loading rate, and either finite-support cell frequencies or a Hölder tensor-spline or wavelet learner supplies the stated covariance rate. Gap inference evaluates explicit directional derivatives on a cross-fitted projected-score sieve.

target_estimand: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1]\) for any \(Q\in\mathcal M\) inducing \(P\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 establishes identification, Theorem 4.2 establishes asymptotic normality, and Remark 4.6 minimizes variance over constant componentwise clean-comparison weights.

Theorem 3.2 derives the covariate-specific optimal efficient influence function and efficiency bound for staggered DiD, while Theorem 4.1 establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and attainment for the resulting estimator.

Theorem 2 identifies the panel DDD target, Theorem 3 identifies the repeated-cross-section target, Theorem 5 derives the panel efficient influence function, and Theorem 7 derives the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function.
Theorem 5.2 gives variance-minimizing conditional GMM instruments when the conditional covariance is singular and a consistent linear system exists.
Theorem 6.3 derives a fixed-weight stacked-DDD limit law and accounts for dependence from comparison units shared across stacks.
The paper derives an efficient imputation estimator under its event-study model and notes applications to triple-difference designs.
Theorem 3.1 establishes asymptotic linearity and Gaussian approximation for cross-fitted estimators based on orthogonal scores.

tldr: The target is a fixed finite aggregate of staggered-DDD group--time effects under the conditional-mean no-anticipation and period-by-period one-step clean-comparison restrictions of Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna. The central theorem defines the target, pairwise residual scores, rank, and spectrum entirely from the observed law, proves existence of a compatible full-data extension exactly under the observable clean-comparison equalities, and exhausts the tangent orthocomplement. Conditional generalized least squares then delivers the canonical gradient \(b^{\star}(X)^{\prime}\Psi_P(O)\), including a Moore--Penrose quotient formula for fixed-rank singular covariance. A deterministic foldwise eigenvalue threshold consistently selects the unknown rank, and a perturbation lemma derives the learned loading rate from conditional-covariance learning; fixed-support and Hölder-series regimes make the paper-specific rates concrete. Globally defined Moore--Penrose versions of the published componentwise loading and the best joint constant loading admit an observable projection-residual diagnostic. Exact pointwise equations characterize their efficiency, a bounded binary-covariate family gives the strict gain \(3/512\), and an explicit directional-derivative plus projected-score sieve yields pointwise Wald inference for an observable gap separated from zero.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.2, and Remark 4.6) establish identification, pairwise-score asymptotic normality, and constant componentwise GMM optimality but leave semiparametric efficiency in overidentified DDD models open. The closest staggered-DiD efficiency result proves observational equivalence before projecting, and the closest DDD influence-function result is just identified.
project_justification.niche: Eligibility creates simultaneous conditional gap equalities and shared cohort--eligibility histories across targets. These features require a DDD-specific full-data extension, tangent-exhaustion argument, and non-block-diagonal conditional covariance operator.
project_justification.fill: The paper first constructs every target, residual, covariance, rank, and spectrum from observed-law primitives, then proves full-data extendability and exact tangent exhaustion. It next derives the fixed-rank canonical gradient and bound, selects the unknown rank by foldwise thresholding, proves covariance and loading rates in discrete and Hölder-series regimes, constructs an attaining cross-fitted estimator, and gives globally defined comparator loadings with an observable equality diagnostic. The efficiency-gap functional has an explicit pathwise derivative, Moore--Penrose KKT contribution, projected-score sieve implementation, and pointwise Wald limit away from equality.

related_work: Ortiz-Villavicencio and Sant'Anna (2025, Theorem 4.1, Theorem 4.2, Remark 4.6, and the conclusion) provide identification under conditional-mean no anticipation and period-by-period one-step DDD parallel trends, pairwise-score asymptotic normality, and the constant within-target GMM benchmark; Theorem 4 of this proposal strictly tightens that benchmark when the pointwise projection equation fails. Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, Lemmas 3.1 and 3.2) inform the observable conditional-moment rotation for single-date and staggered DiD, Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 derive the corresponding optimal conditional efficient influence functions and bounds, and Theorem 4.1 establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and attainment for their estimator. Their DiD model does not supply the DDD-only full-data extension or the tangent-exhaustion proof for coupled eligibility-gap restrictions and shared four-cell histories. Chen and Xie (2026, Sections 2--3 and the full-data extension proofs) clarify why structural identification does not itself establish the observed tangent space. Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami (2025, Theorem 2 for panel identification, Theorem 3 for repeated-cross-section identification, Theorem 5 for the panel efficient influence function, and Theorem 7 for the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function) supply the just-identified reductions; Theorem 11 recovers their panel influence function in the singleton-comparison case. Newey (2001, Theorem 5.2 and its proof) informs the generalized-inverse treatment of redundant conditional moments. Newey (1997) supplies the series-rate and Gram-stability template, while the full shared-cell DDD covariance and thresholded loading rates are established here in discrete and Hölder regimes. Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Theorem 3.1) and Ackerberg et al. (2014) inform the cross-fitting and learned-optimal-weight remainder analysis without being cited as sources of the paper-specific conditional-covariance rates. Hsieh (2026, Section 6) accounts for shared-unit covariance under fixed stacked weights and is a covariance benchmark rather than a target claimed to ignore dependence. Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess (2024) obtain efficiency under a different imputation event-study model; no equivalence to the OVS target-indexed conditional DDD model is asserted. The constant-loading CausalSmith parent is internal prior work and is not cited as published evidence.
technical_internal_limitation: The early-kill calculation must parameterize the complete finite-support tangent matrix for the binary-\(X\), three-score witness under both conditional clean-cohort equalities. Projection of the aggregate derivative must equal \(b^{\star}(X)^{\prime}\Psi\) in both strata and reproduce \(3/512\). Any additional normal direction, omitted compatibility restriction, or failure of the full-data extension invalidates the canonical-gradient claim and forces a downgrade to conditional score-class optimality.
honest_scope: The efficiency theorem is pointwise, uses a fixed finite horizon and target set, and imposes the OVS conditional-mean no-anticipation and target-indexed period-by-period one-step DDD restrictions represented in the observed score system. It does not replace these with almost-sure no anticipation, long-difference parallel trends, or restrictions from untargeted group--time cells. Fixed-rank singularity is covered in the quotient space, and the data estimator recovers that rank with a deterministic threshold under separated positive spectrum; uniform inference when rank changes remains open. The OVS and joint constant comparators use global Moore--Penrose minimum-norm conventions. Gap inference uses a computable projected-score sieve and is stated only for \(\Delta_{\mathrm{cmp}}(P)\ge\delta_0>0\), locally stable comparator KKT ranks, and sieve approximation; inference on the equality boundary remains open. If each target has one clean comparison, the construction reduces to the panel-DDD efficient influence function; if \(X\) is degenerate, it reduces to the best constant joint loading.

novelty_justification: The precise novelty is not inverse conditional covariance by itself. OVS's published result minimizes an unconditional covariance over constant weights separately for each group--time target. Chen--Sant'Anna--Xie prove the analogous full efficiency result for DiD only after an observable-law equivalence theorem: their Theorem 3.2 derives the staggered-DiD conditional efficient influence function and bound, and Theorem 4.1 proves estimator attainment. This proposal's strict delta is the DDD-specific equivalence and tangent-exhaustion theorem for simultaneous eligibility-gap restrictions, followed by a joint cross-target conditional projection with shared-cell covariance, a fixed-rank quotient formula, perturbation-derived learned-loading rates, an attaining estimator, globally defined Moore--Penrose comparator diagnostics, and pointwise inference for the conditional-versus-constant efficiency loss. The arXiv target search through September 10, 2026 found no closer all-clean-cohort staggered-DDD efficiency paper; Hsieh's new stacked DDD paper expressly trades efficiency for transparent fixed weights, and Akbari--Kiyavash--Ghassami remains a basic just-identified DDD result.
